.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Seasonable temperatures and dry through Monday,
then rain chances return late next week.

Strong surface high remains in place across the region through the 
start of next week. Seasonal temperatures and dry conditions are 
expected through Monday as highs reach the 60s, and lows settle in 
the upper 30s to 40s each day. Passing high cirrus today gives way 
to more mid-level cloudiness Sunday due to a shortwave trough that 
slides south of the region. The surface high moves offshore Monday 
and remains centered east of the Mid-Atlantic coast through the 
middle of next week. Return of east to southeast winds bring a 
gradual warming trend next week that has highs reach the low 70s on 
Tuesday, though still remaining dry. 

A deep upper level trough pivots eastward from central CONUS on 
Wednesday, with precipitation chances returning to the forecast 
area. At the surface, a low pressure system tracks from the 
Mississippi River valley towards the Mid-Atlantic the second half of 
the week. As the system approaches, precipitation chances increase 
and are expected to linger through the end of the week. The best 
chance for widespread rain is on Thursday afternoon into Friday, as 
the low pressure system passes nearby. Surface high pressure builds 
overhead in the wake of the low pressure system, with diminishing 
rain chances expected. High temperatures will be in the upper 60s to 
low 70s east of the Blue Ridge with those along and west in the 
upper 50s to 60s. Overnight low temperatures will be in the 50s each 
night. Lows drop into the 40s east of the Blue Ridge Thursday and 
Friday night.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
VFR and dry conditions are expected to prevail through the middle of 
the upcoming week. High pressure over the region will maintain light 
north winds today that gradually turn east to southeast Sunday, then 
remain south through Wednesday. The next chance for showers could 
arrive Wednesday night, but conditions likely still remain VFR.

&&

.MARINE...
Winds will gradually become light to calm this evening into 
tonight as high pressure settles over the region. The high 
begins to move offshore Sunday, then remains centered over the 
western Atlantic through the middle of next week. Light east to 
southeast winds on Sunday become southerly for much of next 
week. Southerly channeling effects could cause some increase in 
winds come Wednesday.
